title: Working with text
lesson:
A string is a row of characters, and each has a position called an **index**, starting at 0. In `word = "Nairobi"`, `word[0]` is "N", `word[1]` is "a", and `word[-1]` (counting from the end) is "i".

**Slicing** takes a piece: `word[0:4]` is "Nair" (from 0 up to, but not including, 4). Leave a side out to go to the edge: `word[:3]` is "Nai", `word[3:]` is "robi".

Strings have **methods**, actions you call with a dot:
- `s.upper()`, `s.lower()`, `s.title()`: change capitals
- `s.strip()`: remove spaces from both ends (people type extra spaces all the time)
- `s.replace("a", "b")`: swap text
- `s.split(",")`: cut into a list of pieces; `", ".join(pieces)` glues a list back
- `s.startswith("07")`, `"ma" in s`: check things
- `s.count("a")`, `s.find("x")`

Strings never change in place: methods give you a **new** string. `name.upper()` alone does nothing you can see; `name = name.upper()` keeps the result.

example.code:
word = "Nairobi"
print(word[0], word[-1], word[:4], word[4:])
name = "  amina odhiambo "
clean = name.strip().title()
print(clean)
print("maize,beans,kale".split(","))
print(" | ".join(["a", "b", "c"]))
print("07" in "0712345678", "Nairobi".lower().count("i"))
notes: Index, last, first four, the rest.

exercises.title: Initials
exercises.prompt: Write initials(full_name): "Amina Wanjiru Odhiambo" gives "A.W.O." Use split.
hints: Each part's first letter is part[0]; make it upper().
Loop over parts adding part[0].upper() + "." to a result string, or use "".join(p[0].upper() + "." for p in parts).
exercises.solution:
def initials(full_name):
    return "".join(p[0].upper() + "." for p in full_name.split())

exercises.title: Safaricom number?
exercises.prompt: Write is_kenyan_mobile(s): True if, after removing spaces, the number is 10 digits starting with 07 or 01, or 13 characters starting with +2547 or +2541. Otherwise False.

tests.hint_if_fail: Check that the rest are all digits: s[1:].isdigit()

hints: len(s), s.startswith(("07", "01")) and s.isdigit() are your tools.
Two cases joined with or: (len(s) == 10 and s.startswith(("07","01")) and s.isdigit()) or (len(s) == 13 and s.startswith(("+2547","+2541")) and s[1:].isdigit())

quiz.why: From index 1 up to (not including) 4: o, m, b.
upper() returns a new string; it wasn't saved.

cards.q: Do string methods change the string?
cards.a: No: they return a new one. Save it: s = s.strip().

bridge: Strings use slicing: `s[0:4]`, `s[-1]`. Compare text with `==` (it compares the letters in Python). Methods: `.strip()`, `.upper()`, `.split()`, `", ".join(...)`.
explain: Explain working with text to someone who has never programmed, in your own words, with an example you make up (not one from the lesson).
